items.briefing:
Ransomware groups are increasingly targeting insiders — employees or contractors — to gain access to organisations, meaning threats can come from within your own workplace, not just outside. Separately, the FBI is investigating a service selling over 153 million stolen drivers licence records, which may affect Australians with US exposure. New AI risk guidance has also been published locally by the Actuaries Institute and UTS for financial services organisations, reflecting growing attention on managing AI-related risks in regulated sectors.

As ransomware tactics evolve to exploit trusted people rather than just technical weaknesses, it's worth reminding staff: if someone — even a colleague — asks you to bypass a security process or share login details, report it immediately to your IT or security team.

featured.title: Microsoft revamps responsible AI rules amid agentic risks
featured.summary: Faster agentic AI adoption is forcing tighter oversight, with new controls on permissions, monitoring and cyber-risk systems.
